description: The agent's comparative model of programming languages. Each language is a ProgrammingLanguage graph node with properties (speed/gc/safety/maturity/etc) the cortex queries to pick a language for an authoring task. Update an attr → the answer changes; add a language → it shows up in the picker. No hardcoded language preferences in code.

languages.name: rust
languages.delivery_format: Cargo-buildable `src/lib.rs` (no extra files). Export FFI symbols with `#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn` matching the benchmark signature exactly so the cortex can dlsym + benchmark.
languages.prompt_toolkit_hint: compiler-theory vocabulary in scope — favour constant folding, identity elimination, strength reduction, common-subexpression elimination, dead-code elimination, reassociation, SIMD intrinsics, wrapping arithmetic for FFI safety.

languages.name: c
languages.delivery_format: Single `.c` file with declarations + definitions; gcc -shared cdylib. Exported functions use the benchmark signature directly (extern "C" wrappers if mixed with C++).
languages.prompt_toolkit_hint: compiler-theory vocabulary in scope — favour constant folding, strength reduction, CSE, dead-code elimination. Manual memory layout permitted; mind aliasing when restricting.

languages.name: cpp
languages.delivery_format: Single `.cpp` file with `extern "C"` wrappers around the benchmark-signature entry points; g++ -shared cdylib.
languages.prompt_toolkit_hint: compiler-theory vocabulary in scope plus templates + constexpr. Mind ABI at the FFI boundary.

languages.name: zig
languages.delivery_format: Single Zig source file exporting the benchmark-signature entry points via `export fn`; built with `zig build-lib -dynamic`.
languages.prompt_toolkit_hint: compiler-theory vocabulary in scope plus comptime metaprogramming. Explicit allocators; no hidden control flow.

languages.name: go
languages.delivery_format: Single Go file exposing the benchmark-signature entry points via cgo `//export` directives.
languages.prompt_toolkit_hint: stdlib + goroutines. Avoid allocations on hot paths; GC pauses dominate microbenchmarks.

languages.name: python
languages.delivery_format: Single `.py` module exposing the named entry-point with the baseline's ABI; standard `import` / `def` / `class`. Stdlib + the listed frameworks only; no extra files.
languages.prompt_toolkit_hint: ML vocabulary in scope — tensors, linear/relu/embedding/attention layers, softmax+cross-entropy, Adam/SGD optimizers (per the listed frameworks). numpy vectorization for non-ML paths; avoid Python-level loops on hot work.
